description: Report cites one real, gold-relevant transaction alongside one fabricated id that doesn't exist in the case.
report_text: N100 sent funds to M201 (T1-001), corroborated by T3-999.
flag: RESOLVED (fix #4): this fixture used to show precision/recall/F1 all reading a PERFECT 1.0 despite the report citing a fabricated id, because the metric's only precision denominator was 'grounded' citations (cited AND real), excluding fabrication entirely. The metric now reports precision two ways, both tested, neither silently conflated: 'precision'/'f1' (standard IR definition, matching the framework's own EP_i = |E_i^agent (all cited) ∩ E_i*| / |E_i^agent| formula) now correctly drops to 0.5/0.6667 here because the fabricated citation counts against the denominator. 'valid_evidence_precision'/'valid_evidence_f1' preserve the ORIGINAL formula (matched / real citations only) under an explicit name, so a caller who deliberately wants precision conditional on non-fabricated citations still has it, unchanged. See docs/evidence-traceability-framework.md#evidence-precision-ep. Either way, 'no fabrication' must never be inferred from a high precision number alone without also checking fabricated_citation_count -- valid_evidence_precision is defined to be blind to it by design.
